how.title: You approve, the AI writes, you decide.

steps.lead: First, record what your company does.
steps.call: Customer service collects name, email, and phone number. Five-year retention. Legal basis: contract performance.
steps.response: Once approved, the record becomes context only for your workspace.

steps.call: Draft the customer service impact assessment report.
steps.response: The AI searches for approved excerpts and drafts using only them. Any element without a basis is declared incomplete.
Once approved, the text is locked. Who did what remains in the audit trail, which the database prevents from being altered.

how.archive: Only what is approved gets filed.

docBody: Customer support collects name, email and phone number to answer tickets.
The data is stored for five years, with encryption at rest.
Access is restricted to the support team, and every lookup is logged.

items.text: Specific role for the Data Protection Officer
Incidents with deadlines for ANPD and data subjects
Elements of the European impact assessment

proof.title: When there was a basis, it found it. When there was none, it refused.
proof.text: In a controlled test with 40 synthetic documents, all 30 searches found the correct excerpt and all 6 questions without a basis were refused. It measures the mechanism and does not guarantee results with real data.

items.a: The model is instructed to use only approved excerpts and to refuse when they are insufficient. This reduces the risk but does not eliminate it. Therefore, all generated text undergoes human review and approval.

items.q: Does IABill replace a lawyer or a DPO?
items.a: No. It organizes the process and prepares documents. The generated texts do not have formal legal validation, and the final decision always rests with your company.

items.q: Can another company see my data?
items.a: Each operation verifies if the resource belongs to your organization, and the AI's search is restricted to your workspace. This isolation is part of the automated tests.

items.q: Is it suitable for companies in Europe?
items.a: Yes. Each workspace defines the applicable regimes, LGPD, GDPR, or both, and the impact assessment report includes the elements of Art. 35 of the GDPR.
Any user can review, and approval is reserved for the administrator profile. Once approved, the content can no longer be edited or regenerated.
